items.summary: Security disposition: evidence_needed for fleet-wide clearance; blocked for public exposure and security-sensitive releases; conditional for ordinary reversible growth. Fleet-doctor has no run or control results, and operations deploy-health, uptime, and error sweeps have no results. Authentication boundaries, least privilege, secrets handling, runtime isolation, release approvals and provenance, dependency and supply-chain controls, data exposure, monitoring, incident response, complete TLS posture, and security.txt/disclosure readiness remain unverified. No certificates are reported expiring within 30 days, but that does not prove complete TLS coverage. Compliance is a technical baseline only: 37 pass, 15 fail, and 7 unknown, with open banner, consent, analytics, privacy, and terms findings. Retained worker and reviewer failures are containment signals, not evidence of exploitation. Exact decision: preserve private launch gates; permit only bounded reversible work that preserves existing consent, disclosures, data handling, claims, and access boundaries. Do not create or requeue production work, access credentials or private containers, modify permissions or configuration, add dependencies, deploy, request duplicate telemetry, or conduct external outreach.

Retain containment-only execution. Continue the existing read-only security evidence matrix using authorized metadata and retained artifacts, with dated redacted evidence, affected scope, owners, explicit unknowns, severity, and release implications. Continue existing repair-or-close, attribution reconciliation, and measurement work only; keep all private gates unchanged.
